summary: Set up PostgreSQL 13 streaming replication across node1 (initial primary), node2 and node3 (standbys) on AlmaLinux 9, using pg_basebackup -R with a dedicated replicator role (SCRAM-SHA-256) and opened firewalld port 5432. Demonstrated failover: stopped node1's postgres, promoted node2 via pg_ctl promote (timeline advanced to 2), repointed node3's primary_conninfo to node2, verified zero committed-data loss (all pre-failover rows present on both survivors, new writes accepted by node2). Rebuilt node1 from a fresh pg_basebackup against node2 and brought it back online as a standby of the new primary, restoring the 3-node topology (node2 primary, node1/node3 standbys) with all historical rows intact. Then ran the mandatory node-restart protocol on all three nodes one at a time (node1, node3, node2/primary last) using systemctl reboot backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect; confirmed each node's boot_id changed, PostgreSQL came back active, replication/recovery role was correct, and a final write on the primary replicated to both standbys after every node had been restarted.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server/contrib 13.23 on node1, node2, node3
Initialized DB on node1; configured wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders, hot_standby, pg_hba.conf replication rules, password_encryption=[REDACTED]
Created replicator role with SCRAM password generated via openssl on node1; distributed to node2/node3 via root SSH scp using cluster keypair, never printed in transcript
Opened firewalld 5432/tcp on all three nodes (was blocking replication connections)
Cloned node1 to node2 and node3 via pg_basebackup -R; started both as standbys and confirmed streaming state with identical replayed baseline data
Inserted baseline and pre-failover committed rows on node1 primary; confirmed replay on both standbys before disruption
Simulated primary loss: systemctl stop postgresql on node1
Promoted node2 to writable primary via pg_ctl promote; verified pg_is_in_recovery=false and all pre-failover rows present (no data loss); wrote new row to confirm writability
Repointed node3's primary_conninfo to node2 and reloaded config; observed timeline switch to 2 and continued streaming; confirmed node3 had all rows including the post-failover write
Rebuilt node1 via fresh pg_basebackup against node2, started it as a standby of node2; verified full data set present
Confirmed final 3-node topology (node2 primary, node1+node3 standbys) with a new write replicated to both

Ran mandatory restart protocol: captured boot_id + service/replication health baseline on all nodes; restarted node1, then node3, then node2 (primary) one at a time via backgrounded systemctl reboot; polled each until reachable; verified changed boot_id, active postgresql, correct recovery role, and intact replicated data on each after restart
Confirmed final post-restart write from node2 replicated to node1 and node3
Cleaned up temporary /tmp/.repl_pw credential copies from all nodes

evidence.requirement: Primary/standby replication topology established (node1 primary, node2+node3 standbys) with streaming confirmed
evidence.summary: node1 initialized and started as primary; node2 and node3 cloned via pg_basebackup -R and started, both showing pg_is_in_recovery=true; pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both standbys streaming

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline data replicated identically to both standbys before disruption
evidence.summary: Rows inserted on node1 primary (baseline-1, baseline-2, pre-failover-committed) and confirmed present with matching WAL replay LSN on both node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: Primary loss simulated and standby promoted without losing committed data
evidence.summary: node1 postgres stopped; node2 promoted via pg_ctl promote (pg_is_in_recovery=false); all 3 pre-failover rows present on node2 plus a new post-failover write accepted, proving writability with no data loss

evidence.requirement: Surviving standby (node3) repointed to new primary and remains consistent
evidence.summary: node3 primary_conninfo updated to node2, config reloaded, log shows timeline switch to 2 and restarted WAL streaming; node3 data confirmed to include all 4 rows including the post-failover write; node2 pg_stat_replication shows node3 streaming

evidence.requirement: Recovered former primary (node1) rejoins as standby of the new primary with data restored
evidence.summary: node1 rebuilt via pg_basebackup from node2, started as standby (pg_is_in_recovery=true) with all rows present; node2 confirmed streaming to both node1 and node3; a new write on node2 replicated to both, completing the required post-failover topology

Baseline boot_id 9bdcc129 captured with postgres active/in-recovery; systemctl reboot issued and acked; connection reset confirmed disruption; new boot_id 3e284772 confirms actual restart; post-restart postgres active, standby role and full 5-row dataset confirmed
Baseline boot_id dfdea52d captured; reboot issued; connection timeout confirms disruption; new boot_id a5bc1f6a confirms restart; post-restart postgres active, standby role and full dataset confirmed

Baseline boot_id f43afa1c captured with node2 as primary streaming to both standbys reconfirmed just before restart; reboot issued; connection timeout confirms disruption; new boot_id 3341601e confirms restart; post-restart node2 still primary with both standbys reconnected and streaming, full dataset intact

evidence.requirement: Full cluster health and data consistency after all three restarts
evidence.summary: Final write on node2 (primary) after all restarts replicated to both node1 and node3, confirmed by count query on each
